Alexandria approves plan to update helmet requirements for e-bikes, scooters

By Scott Gelman
November 16, 2026 | 2:48 PM
|
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 2:28
Instaread

Kids riding electric bikes and scooters in Alexandria, Virginia, will be required to wear a helmet, as part of an update to city rules approved last weekend.

The city’s current law calls for anyone 14 and under riding a bike to wear a helmet. Now, that law expands the requirement to include riders in that same age bracket on power-assisted bikes, motorized skateboards, electric personal assistive mobility devices and motorized scooters and bikes.

Thomas Hillman, who works with the city’s transportation and environmental services’ mobility services division, told city leaders last week the change aimed to help “stay consistent with the state-enabling legislation for local youth helmet ordinances.”

The update comes after Virginia’s General Assembly amended the state code during its 2026 legislative session. The step added motorized scooters and skateboards to the list of devices a local jurisdiction could require a helmet for, for riders 14 years old and younger.

The approved change keeps in tact the $25 civil penalty for kids found to not be wearing a helmet while riding a bike, e-bike or e-scooter. Based on Virginia law, that fine can be suspended for someone’s first violation or for subsequent violations once there is proof they have a helmet.

A violator’s parent or guardian is responsible for the fine, based on state law.

Council member Abdel-Rahman Elnoubi said during the Nov. 10 meeting that he’s “excited” the plan passed and added it’s an important step because, “We see a lot of youth riding scooters and all of that, with and without helmets.”

Related stories:

  • Some e-bikes can hit 50 mph. Officials say they don’t belong on the W&OD Trail
  • Vienna police warn parents about e-bikes modifications kids are making
  • School resource officers to visit Loudoun County parents over e-bike safety for youth

Broadly, Elnoubi recommended the city have future conversations about scooter use, because, “I’ve heard from a lot of residents about scooters ridden on the sidewalk, especially by youth, sometimes two and three youth at a time riding a scooter. And I know there’s also a certain age where they shouldn’t be renting scooters under, but it’s happening.”

Vice Mayor Sarah Bagley, meanwhile, said the city’s chief race and social equity officer found the policy update would not have an inequitable impact, but the city should ensure the helmet requirement “does not become a barrier to entry to those using those devices.”

The updated rules go into effect immediately.

Flyers face long baggage waits at Reagan National Airport following United Airlines outage, recent FAA ground stop

By Anna-Lysa Gayle
November 16, 2026 | 10:19 PM
|
Some passengers at Reagan National Airport experienced issues retrieving their bags from baggage claim Monday evening. United Airlines experienced a technology-related outage Monday, causing hiccups for some flyers. This comes after a nationwide ground stop Friday. “Earlier today we experienced a technology-related issue that impacted some departing flights. The issue has been resolved,” United said on X. Uche Nwankwo said he waited more than seven hours at the airport after his flight from Houston, Texas, arrived just before noon.
